It is limited to a single continuous patch in the southernmost part of the county, as well as some sparser regions in the east. Much of the county is occupied by a series of canyons and steep terrain, which end abruptly at the brook cliffs, creating a semi-circle of flatter land. The significant lack of cooling water in more than half of the county stacks on to the slope limitations to create a very small window of viability for large LWRs. The relaxed slope restriction seems to open up more of the eastern portion of the county not occupied by canyons for siting of water-cooled SMR technology, as can be seen in Table U.C2. Much more of this region would be viable if not for a large swatch of protected land in the far east. Depending on the nature of the protected land, there may also be unforeseen difficulties accessing cooling water from the Green river, which flanks Carbon County’s eastern border. In Table U.C3, the removal of the need for cooling water creates a much larger region of suitability occupying most of the basin below the Brook Cliffs. This change also opens up a relatively contiguous region in the northernmost part of Carbon County. There is only a single major population center in Carbon County that excludes some of the basin, which is the city of Price. Unlike many of the other regions in this analysis, the geography of Carbon County even excludes large portions of land from data center siting, as seen in Table U.C4. With that said, there is still a significant amount of available land throughout the county, which coincides well with potential nuclear sites, which is evident in Table U.C5. As with many other regions, the widespread availability of suitable land for data center siting means that the limiting factor in the collocation question is suitable land for nuclear development. 57 Table U.C1: Data Package for Large Light Water Reactor for Carbon Utah Large LWR (e.g., AP1000) Green –Meets all Criteria Yellow –Single issue Orange –Two issues Blue –3+ issues Composite Map Basemap 58 Individual Excluded Area Population (>500 ppsm within 20 miles) SSE (>0.3g) Wetlands/Open Waters Protected Lands Slope (>12% grade) Landslide Risk (High Risk Areas) Floodplain (100-year Risk Areas) Streamflow (<130,000 gpm) Proximity to Hazards Proximity to Fault Lines 59 Table U.C2: Data Package for Small Modular Reactor for Carbon Utah Small Modular Reactor (e.g., AP300) Green –Meets all Criteria Yellow –Single issue Orange –Two issues Blue –3+ issues Composite Map Basemap 60 Individual Excluded Area Population (>500 ppsm within
